method: agent visual audit of audit_crops/*.jpg + audit_sheet_*.jpg (each sampled point projected into the best-visible real capture photo, E4 replay refined pose + patched K, RAW 3840x2160 coords - same projection recipe E4 colorize verified at median |dRGB|~8). Labels: TRUE_KILL = killed point is a physically-impossible / specular-ghost point (correct kill); REAL = point is real scene geometry; AMB = specular-capable surface, cannot exclude reflected content. Single-rater (E7 agent), NOT user-approved ground truth. Sampling seeded (7), rule already frozen before audit - no feedback into the rule.

findings.F1_bh8_validated: zero audited true-geometry kills at bh=8 on both caps (0/98 kept-side audited points wrongly killed; 48/48 audited kills correct); the bh sweep is FLAT for bh>=7 (cap40 310 culls for bh 7..12; cap41 387 for bh 8..12), so bh=8 sits on a robust plateau, not a scene-tuned knife-edge; and the bh3-differential audit (35/35 REAL) independently reproduces the cap50 red line that forced bh>=8. No operating-point drift.
findings.F2_belowfloor_path1_leak_NEW: the E3 claim 'below-floor standing oppose = constructive 100% annihilation' does NOT fully transfer: path-1 (>=3 recovered obs) outranks the below-floor veto in the frozen rule, and planar-mirror virtual points can be multiview-consistent. cap40 keeps 18/49 (37%) below-floor points, cap41 163/373 (44%), median fh -0.15, all via keep_risk_multiview (cap50/51 had zero such points, so E3 never saw this). Audited samples look like glossy-floor reflection ghosts. This is NOT a bh=8 issue (corridor vote untouched); flagged as a candidate rule refinement (below-floor veto should arguably outrank path-1) that would be a RULE CHANGE requiring separate sign-off - E7 did not apply it.
findings.F3_corridor_inert_in_bedroom: at bh=8 the corridor net-visibility vote adds ZERO kills beyond the below-floor veto in this scene (all 27/202 E3-risk kills are cull_risk_belowfloor); its cleaning value (deep-penetration mirror trails) remains demonstrated only on cap50; in the bedroom its role is purely protective (not killing real geometry), which it passes.
